hook: Bernhard Schölkopf studied physics, mathematics and philosophy in Tübingen and London, then completed a doctorate in computer science at the Technical University of Berlin in 1997. He worked at the German National Research Center for Computer Science and held industrial research posts at AT&T Bell Laboratories, Microsoft Research and Biowulf Technologies, a period in which he helped develop the kernel methods that underlie the support vector machine framework used widely in machine learning. In 2001 he became a director and scientific member at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics, and since 2011 he has directed the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Tübingen. His research has shifted toward causal machine learning, arguing that statistical learning methods need causal structure to generalize reliably outside their training distribution, work recognized with the 2019 Körber Prize. He also holds an honorary professorship at TU Berlin.
